[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==

'''Nancy Glasgow''' was born about 1820–1821. She later lived at Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, where she died before January 1892, probably on 31 October 1891.

No record names Nancy's parents. The January 1892 probate citation lists children of John, Alexander and Robert Glasgow, Jane Dysart, Ann McClelland and Mary Thompson, and names David, James and Samuel Anderson at Gortahar among the cited heirs or next of kin. It does not name Elizabeth as their mother; her identification comes from other family records. The citation, Nancy's explicit niece and nephew statements in her will, and the Irish family records support a '''probable sibling network''' associated with Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. The notice does not expressly state every sibling relationship or establish that the list is complete.<ref name="NancyCitation" />

The '''John Glasgow, farmer''' named as father in the 1846 marriage of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] is a candidate for Nancy's father only if the proposed siblings shared that parent. Full and half-sibling relationships remain unresolved. The proposed father represented by [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow]] is not thereby identified with the 1796 Desertoghill flax-premium recipient. Nancy was earlier attached to [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-761034|Rosanna Unknown]]; that parentage remains unproved, but omission of Thomas's or Daniel's family from the citation does not disprove it. Neither their absence nor the probable sibling network establishes a replacement father. No mother has been identified.<ref name="NancyCitation" />

=== Plattsburgh and Will ===

On 15 January 1889 Nancy made her Last Will and Testament at Plattsburgh. She described herself as '''unmarried''' and '''about 68 years old''', suggesting a birth about 1820–1821.<ref name="NancyWill">Clinton County, New York, Surrogate's Court, ''Records of wills, 1807–1902'', vol. Q, pp. 255–259, Nancy Glasgow of Plattsburgh; will dated 15 January 1889, admitted to probate 9 May 1892. FamilySearch catalogue, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/319520 Records of wills, 1807–1902].</ref>

Nancy signed the will by making her mark. Her witnesses were '''D. C. Boynton''' and '''E. S. Winslow''', both of Plattsburgh. When they appeared before the Surrogate in 1892 they testified that they had known Nancy personally, that she was of sound mind when she executed the will, and that she was a citizen of the United States.<ref name="NancyWill" />

She appointed '''Hiram Walworth''' of Plattsburgh as executor and gave him authority to sell or reinvest her property as necessary to carry out the provisions of the will.<ref name="NancyWill" />

=== Relatives Named in the Will ===

Nancy explicitly identified several relatives:

* '''[[Anderson-104744|Robert Anderson]]''', deceased, whom she called her '''nephew''';
* '''[[Anderson-104750|Dinah Anderson]]''', widow of Robert Anderson;
* '''[[Anderson-104751|Robert Wallace Anderson]]''', whom Nancy also called her '''nephew''', and whose mother was Dinah Anderson;
* '''[[Dysart-1890|Margaret (Dysart) Kennedy]]''' of West Troy, New York, whom Nancy called her '''niece'''.<ref name="NancyWill" />

Nancy directed her executor to retain '''$500''' in trust for Robert Wallace Anderson until he reached the age of 21. If he died before that age, the money and accumulated interest were to pass to his mother Dinah.<ref name="NancyWill" />

She left '''$200''' to Dinah Anderson and '''$200''' to Margaret Kennedy. The residue of her estate was left to Dinah Anderson or her legal representatives.<ref name="NancyWill" />

Other legacies included:

* $100 to the Woman's Union Missionary Society of America for Heathen Lands;
* $50 to the trustees of the Peristrome Presbyterian Church of Plattsburgh;
* $50 to Ann Cavanagh, wife of John Cavanagh of Plattsburgh;
* $50 to Alexander Weir of Plattsburgh;
* $50 collectively to Carrie B. Walworth, Graham H. Walworth, Clarence B. Walworth, Mary E. Walworth and Lottie Place of St. Albans, Vermont.<ref name="NancyWill" />

=== Death and Probate ===

A transcription of Riverside Cemetery at Plattsburgh records a '''Nancy Glasgow''' as dying on '''31 October 1891'''. This is a strong candidate for the testator, although the original gravestone or cemetery register has not yet been examined.<ref name="Riverside">Northern New York Tombstone Transcription Project, [https://nnytombstoneproject.nygenweb.net/clinton/plattsburgh/riverside_a_k.htm Riverside Cemetery, Plattsburgh, A–K], entry for Nancy Glasgow, reporting death 31 October 1891.</ref>

Nancy was certainly deceased by '''14 January 1892''', when the Clinton County Surrogate issued a citation concerning probate of her will.<ref name="NancyCitation">''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'' (Plattsburgh, New York), 26 February 1892, p. 6, "Legal Notices", probate citation in the estate of Nancy Glasgow, dated 14 January 1892; [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 digital newspaper page].</ref>

Her will was formally admitted to probate on '''9 May 1892''' by Clinton County Surrogate '''David F. Dobie''' and recorded in Will Book Q, pages 255–259.<ref name="NancyWill" />

=== Probate Citation and Extended Family ===

The 1892 probate citation provides considerable evidence for Nancy's wider family network, although it does not state the exact relationship between Nancy and most of the people named.

Among those cited were:

* '''James G. Glasgow, Ann and Lizzie''', children of '''John Glasgow''', formerly of Baladonly, County Antrim, Ireland;
** Probable match [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow (abt.1801-1895)]], whose marriage names his father as John Glasgow, farmer; identification of that father with [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow (1751-abt.1852)]] remains unproved.
* '''James Glasgow, Mary and Ann''', children of '''Alexander Glasgow''', formerly of Rasharkin, County Antrim, Ireland;
** Best match [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow (abt.1811-1888)]] who has children James, Mary and Ann. 
* '''Mary Jane and Ann''', children of '''Robert Glasgow''';
** [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow (abt.1779-abt.1852)]] or [[Glasgow-1049|Robert Glasgow Sr (abt.1811-abt.1888)]], altho neither are a good fit, maybe [[Glasgow-4049|Robert Glasgow (abt.1849-)]]? 
* '''[[Dysart-232|Robert Dysart]]''' of Rasharkin and '''[[Dysart-1225|James Dysart]]''';
* '''Sallie''', daughter of '''[[Glasglow-11|Jane Catherine (Glasglow) Dysart]]''', of Ballymena;
* '''[[Dysart-1845|Mary Jane (Dysart) Hampton]]''', another daughter of Jane Dysart, believed to be living in Canterbury, New Zealand;
* '''Martha Dysart''' and '''Elizabeth Weir''', both living in Canterbury, New Zealand;
* '''[[Dysart-1890|Margaret (Dysart) Kennedy]]''' of West Troy, New York;
* '''David Anderson, James Anderson and Samuel Anderson''' of Gortahar, County Antrim;
* the unnamed children of '''Ann McClelland''';
* the unnamed children of '''Mary Thompson'''.<ref name="NancyCitation" />

The citation describes these people collectively within proceedings involving Nancy's "heirs or next of kin", but it does '''not''' state that John, Alexander and Robert Glasgow were Nancy's brothers, nor does it identify Nancy as a daughter of any of them. Their precise relationships remain under investigation.<ref name="NancyCitation" />

The Alexander Glasgow identified in the notice as formerly of Rasharkin may be connected with the documented Glasgow family of Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish. However, this notice alone does not establish that he was Nancy's brother. The combined will and Irish household evidence supports that relationship as probable.

In the 1870 U.S. census, '''Nancy Glascow''', aged 50 and born in Ireland, was living in Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, with '''Delia Walworth'''. The household connection is consistent with Nancy’s later appointment of Hiram Walworth as executor and bequests to Walworth children; it establishes a close Plattsburgh association, not Irish Glasgow kinship. The age, birthplace, residence and spelling variation strongly fit this Nancy, but the census does not name her parents or establish her relationship to Alexander Glasgow.<ref name="Nancy1870">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M8FF-ZQD FamilySearch], U.S. census, 1870, Nancy Glascow, Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, record M8FF-ZQD, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

=== 1860–1880 Walworth Household Continuity ===

FamilySearch records show a long-term Plattsburgh association between Nancy and the Walworth household, although the census ages vary and the relationship is not identified as kinship. In the 1860 U.S. census, '''Nancy Glascoe''', age 30 and born in Ireland, was enumerated in The Village of Plattsburgh in the household of Hiram Walworth, Cornelia L. Walworth, Delia A. Walworth and others. In 1870, '''Nancy Glascow''', age 50 and born in Ireland, was living with Delia Walworth. In 1880, '''Nancy Glasgow''', age 65 and born in Ireland, was living in Plattsburgh with Delia A. Walworth and Alice C. Walworth; she was recorded as single, a servant, and "Other" in relation to the head of household. This repeated association helps explain Nancy’s later appointment of Hiram Walworth as executor and bequests to Walworth children. It strengthens the identification of the Plattsburgh Nancy, but it does not prove that she was related to Alexander Glasgow or to Mary and Ann.

<ref name="Nancy1860">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MC7C-HHK FamilySearch], U.S. census, 1860, Nancy Glascoe, The Village of Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, record MC7C-HHK, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
<ref name="Nancy1880">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MZZF-HDJ FamilySearch], U.S. census, 1880, Nancy Glasgow, Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, record MZZF-HDJ, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

=== Clinton County Probate Index and Petition Trail ===

FamilySearch's Clinton County probate index lists Nancy Glasgow with a death date of 31 October 1891, residence in Plattsburgh, and a testate estate; the representative is identified as Hiram Walworth. A separate FamilySearch transcript from the Clinton County guardianship and probate records for 1892–1898 records the estate as Nancy Glasgow, then lists a petition filed by Hiram Walworth as executor named for probate of the will, an order for citation, service by publication, filing of the executor's oath, probate of the will, and issuance of letters testamentary to Hiram Walworth. This confirms the probate trail and identifies the surviving record group most likely to contain the names of Nancy's heirs or next of kin. The available transcript is AI-generated and does not itself state Nancy's relationship to Alexander Glasgow; the original petition and service pages still need to be read.

<ref name="NancyProbateIndex">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9YCX-9W3 FamilySearch], Clinton County, New York, ''Probate Indexes 1807–1969, 1830–1969'', entry for Nancy Glasgow, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
<ref name="NancyProbatePetition">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYCZ-X98 FamilySearch], Clinton County, New York, ''Guardianship Records 1892–1898, Probate Records 1892–1898'', transcript for estate of Nancy Glasgow, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
